description:
## Goal
An eligible public customer can deploy an app, create or attach its database, inject the permitted connection secret, inspect usage/invoices, and recover from provisioning or suspension states through one tested journey.

## Scope
Extend existing onboarding project/deploy/complete steps, application environment/secret controls, and E managed-database customer components/routes. ## Interfaces and ownership

## Implementation details

- Inject the database connection through existing scoped encrypted-secret/environment controls. Offer the E pooled/direct and non-superuser role choices where permitted; never expose credentials to billing-only members, usage logs or browser telemetry.
- Support an existing external Neon/customer-managed database connection through E's standard PostgreSQL contract without forcing a built-in database purchase. Do not add Neon-specific application code.
- Handle failed/slow create, no quota, invalid connection, secret permission loss, resumed session, rotation overlap and rollback of an app binding using E's tested backend operations rather than placeholder success.

title: G3: Open public signup with verified, bounded allocation admission
description:
## Goal
A new public customer can register and prepare an empty project, while compute/database/build allocation remains blocked until verified email and valid payment setup or an approved bounded trial.

## Interfaces and ownership
Consumes existing Better Auth session/email verification/organization interfaces, phase A trial/abuse terms and selected bot-check/shared-limit store, F1 Checkout/summary, F4 trusted eligibility and C allocation service. Produces public registration/verification states, bounded trial/payment admission, shared limiter outcomes, independent abuse restriction causes, and onboarding readiness for G4.

## Implementation details
- Reuse Better Auth verification and mail delivery with explicit hosted mode; preserve unrelated self-hosted behavior. A registration/empty project path does not allocate billable resources.
- Persist and enforce the accepted bounded trial/payment prerequisites server-side. The browser cannot self-declare email verification, a trial, payment completion or budget exemption.
- Reuse Better Auth endpoint rate limiting with a shared store selected in phase A and trusted proxy configuration. Protect relevant tRPC, server-side auth.api and allocation calls separately because client-endpoint limits do not cover them.
- Apply per-account concurrency, organization/signup limits and the canonical platform-wide allocation ceiling through existing C admission. Keep rate limits separate from resource quota reservations.
- Integrate the selected bot check through the existing Better Auth plugin where applicable; reuse its verification/expiry/replay tests from tenancy audit T6. Do not implement a new challenge engine or silently require an unselected paid service.
- Show verification resend/recovery, payment pending/failure, trial terms, the G2 default stop budget, and continuing storage terms at the appropriate existing onboarding steps.
- Add public browser/API flows and shared-store concurrency tests for denied and eligible allocation. Use test mail/provider responses; document actual signup limits, operational failures and support recovery.

- Unverified email, expired/replayed verification, missing payment/trial eligibility and forged Checkout return cannot start builds, app compute or a database through UI, tRPC, direct server-side calls or scheduled jobs.
- After verified identity and a trusted valid payment setup/approved bounded trial, the same customer can pass C/F admission within quotas and the default G2 budget.
- Shared limits hold across at least two control-plane instances; proxy header spoofing, concurrent signups, resend floods and internal auth.api bypass attempts do not avoid the accepted limits.
- Mail failure, challenge/provider outage, missing/replayed token and payment outage produce recoverable visible states without allowing allocation. Payment recovery does not clear an abuse cause.
- Public browser traces, real shared-store/admission evidence, full coverage, customer terms/help and operator procedures pass; no production bulk mail or live payment is sent by the tests.

title: E6: Control database resize, stop, maintenance and deletion with exact usage
description:
## Goal
Database lifecycle changes converge to one observed state while preserving correct capacity reservations, recovery history and usage intervals.

## Scope
Implement selected-backend fixed-size resize/storage growth, explicit stop/start, tested minor updates, restriction/resume and close/delete lifecycle through existing resource operations. Credential rotation remains E3. Integrate exact D meters and F/G-compatible restriction causes without waiting for payment or spend UI.

## Interfaces and ownership
Consumes E1 selected profiles/resources, E2 connections, E3 credential versions, E4 history/retention, E5 restore validation, C1 operations/reservations, C4 execution lease controls and D usage sink/completeness contract. Produces managedDatabase.resize/start/stop/delete/maintenance APIs, generation-checked status, retained storage/backup state, tombstones and exact database-size/storage/backup observations. F/G later invoke these APIs with distinct restriction causes.

## Implementation details
- Reserve size/storage growth atomically, use selected-backend resize/update operations and reconcile acknowledgement loss. State interruption before execution and release old capacity only after observed transition.
- Implement explicit stop/start with separate compute and retained-storage state. Preserve history and last valid backup during suspended-resource retention; do not encode stopped storage as deleted or zero usage.
- Add minor-update procedure for the pinned PostgreSQL18 line with compatible pooler/backup versions, readiness/integrity checks and a tested restore path. Do not perform an unsupported in-place downgrade on changed data files.
- Separate deletion request, compute removal, contracted retained-data/backup period and final removal; preserve immutable resource/audit/usage evidence and secret revocation. Reconcile partial delete/orphan state with generation fences.
- Emit D's immutable exact-unit intervals split at observed running/stop/size/storage and ownership boundaries. Bill database compute once as selected size-time, not again as application CPU/RAM; retained storage and customer backup bytes continue after compute stop.
- Compose payment/budget/abuse/operator causes without one resume clearing another cause. Add interrupted resize/maintenance/delete and stale-collector scenarios plus customer/operator documentation for interruption, retained costs and recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Concurrent/replayed resize cannot exceed quota or apply an obsolete generation; failed/interrupted resize converges to a documented size and preserves a usable database or tested recovery path.
- Stop/start changes compute observation only when verified; storage/backup retention persists and D totals remain exact across the boundary.
- A minor-update rehearsal preserves data, allowed extensions, roles, pool/direct connections and recoverability; incompatible update is rejected before irreversible mutation or leaves the tested restore path.
- Delete/cancel/restart and delayed provider acknowledgement cannot remove another tenant's/newer resource, double-release capacity or delete required billing/audit tombstones.
- Usage fixtures reconcile known running intervals, size changes, retained volumes/objects and deletion with decimal-string/integer quantities; no app CPU/RAM double billing occurs.
- Payment/budget recovery cannot resume a database still restricted for abuse or another independent cause; expired authority and stale metering do not permit new growth.

description:
## Goal
Each retained managed database has observable backup/recovery history that survives compute loss, stop and suspension.

## Scope

## Interfaces and ownership
Consumes E1 resource/profile, C1 durable scheduler/operation identity, E3 scoped secret/key recovery, selected-backend recovery capabilities and D exact backup-storage observation contract. Produces backup/history inventory, last successful backup/WAL times, oldest supported restore point, quality/error state, scoped restore references and exact customer backup-object bytes for D. ## Implementation details
- For operated databases, reuse packaged pgBackRest stanza-create/check/backup/info/verify/expire and its Azure/S3 repository support. Configure continuous WAL, encryption and per-resource repository scope outside the database VM.
- For a provider selection, expose its tested restore-history/backup inventory through the same service boundary and account for required history/support/transfer cost under A5. Do not describe provider backup as our pgBackRest deployment.
- Use C1 durable schedule/operation dispatch, not node-schedule as the hosted authority. Reconcile missed runs, partial uploads, worker restarts and archive errors without expiring the last valid recovery chain.
- Implement the 7-day history policy and preserve at least one valid backup for the full retained-resource lifetime, including 30-day suspension retention. Coordinate pgBackRest/provider retention with object-store lifecycle; compute stop cannot silently remove the last backup.
- Separate scoped archive-write credentials from restore/deletion authority. Protect encryption keys and test recovery from saved keys. Emit exact retained customer object sizes and exclude provider redundancy/platform metadata copies from billable quantity.

title: E3: Bind and rotate database secrets and support external databases
description:
## Goal
An authorized user can attach a managed or external PostgreSQL connection to an application environment and rotate managed credentials without exposing platform secrets.

## Scope

## Interfaces and ownership

E5/E6/E7 consume binding/rotation state; F/G must not grant secret-read access merely for billing.

## Implementation details
- Reuse encryptValue/decryptValue and scoped vault adapters. Add a managed secret read boundary that treats wrong/missing keys or corrupted ciphertext as unavailable; do not inject raw ciphertext from encryptedText's existing fallback.
- Add a reversible expand/backfill/validate path for managed legacy databasePassword values, with secret-free migration evidence and encryption-key backup/restore rules. Phase H owns whole-installation migration rollout; this task supplies the safe per-record migration and fixtures.
- Validate ownership on both database/secret provider and target application/environment before binding. Use existing environment injection and redaction; platform administration secrets never become customer variables.
- Implement request-keyed credential rotation through C1 with new version/role, overlap window, verification, old-version expiry and recovery after partial provider/app update. Preserve independent stop/abuse causes.
- Accept standard secret-backed external PostgreSQL URLs, including Neon and self-managed databases, through the same scoped binding UI/API contract without allocating or metering a managed database. Do not probe arbitrary external hosts from the control plane by default.

title: C1: Make hosted admission and resource operations atomic and durable
description:
## Goal
A permitted request reserves capacity and records exactly one recoverable resource operation in a single PostgreSQL transaction.

## Scope
Productionize the queue/outbox choice from A3 and the hosted-mode, tenant-context, real-PostgreSQL and coverage contracts from phase B. Own canonical hosted admission/entitlement projection, quota reservations, resource-allocation identity, resource-operation state and durable transition delivery. Phase F updates this same admission projection later; it must not create a second quota ledger. Baseline source inspected: 06a14eb130684f1ac9c66dce42de890eb6616184.

## Interfaces and ownership
Consumes authenticated organization/actor/role context, the phase-A catalog and eligibility policy, and B's tenant-scoped transaction/worker roles. Produces reserve-and-enqueue(input object), operation.get(id), claim/renew/complete/cancel with a generation fence, and durable resource transition records carrying event/source identity, organization/project/environment/resource/generation, observed time and exact capacity fields. Jobs contain an operation ID; the worker reloads authoritative ownership/state. D consumes transition observations; F/G consume the admission and lease interfaces.

## Implementation details
- Add proposed resource-allocation.ts and resource-operation.ts schema/service modules and the minimum admission/reservation records needed for their contract. Register schema/server exports and expand migrations; use B's RLS/ownership helpers on every new row and relationship.
- Within one transaction, lock admission records in a documented order, reject unknown/ineligible hosted state, reserve all capacity dimensions, and insert unique request/resource-operation plus selected durable queue/outbox entry. Repeated keys with equal inputs return the same operation; changed inputs conflict.
- Keep native PostgreSQL outbox as the accepted fallback; use only the A3-selected pg-boss/Graphile/native mechanism. Reuse same-transaction enqueue and existing deployment ordering. Do not build a second worker engine or a second reservation authority.
- Implement bounded claim leases, heartbeats, monotonic generation/fence checks, retry state, cancellation and terminal failure. Perform provider calls outside DB transactions. Revalidate organization ownership, admission and generation before side effects and before committing results.
- Persist recoverable transition observations without secrets, with stable identity and sequence through replay; document how D consumes them without billing from sampled charts. Restrict worker DB privileges and audit permission-sensitive transitions.
- Add unit and real-PostgreSQL concurrency/restart tests using B1's integration harness; extend existing queue ordering tests. Document operation states, retry advice, reservation release rules, poison-operation inspection and safe replay in proposed docs/operations/hosted-resource-operations.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Two independent DB connections requesting the last quota slot produce one accepted operation and one quota-exhaustion result; the rejected request creates no cloud call, reservation or billable allocation.
- Transaction rollback leaves neither operation nor queue/outbox work nor reserved capacity. Commit makes all three durable across process restart.
- Duplicate request, delayed worker, expired lease and old generation cannot allocate twice, complete an obsolete operation or release a newer reservation. Double release has no effect.
- A crash before or after external acknowledgement resumes through reconciliation; queue retry is never represented as exactly-once cloud execution.
- Unknown hosted policy, removed membership, forged operation organization and cross-organization resource links fail closed with stable non-disclosing errors; explicit self-hosted behavior retains its prior contract.
- Cancellation and permanent failure have explicit retained-resource/reservation behavior. A pending or ambiguous provider outcome cannot free capacity as if deletion were confirmed.
- operation.get exposes only the authorized resource's asynchronous state; durable transition identities remain stable through replay and contain no credentials.
